main_text.l: detur profecto ista albedo, quæ est accidens, pror-
sus quemadmodum diuiditur illud corpus cui inhæ-
rét:) ita & motus partium simul fieri intelligetur,
quemadmodum fit motus totius rei mobilis.
Quomodo distinguitur motus secun-
dum partes rei mobilis à motu
secundum tempus?
Hoc pacto: Quando diuiditur motus secundum
partes rei mobilis, ipsæ partes simul manent: quan-
do vero diuiditur motus secundum tempus, tum par-
tes non manent simul. Si tamen motus partis unius
comparetur ad partem alterius, non simpliciter, sed
secundum certum aliquod signum, ad quod fit mo-
tus, sanè hic motus unius partis etiam tempore præce-
det motum alterius. c Sumatur (uerbi gratia)
res mobilis A ⌐——⌙——⌐ B. & moueatur in
G magnitudine E ⌐——⌙——⌐ F. ita ut magnitu-
do E G æqualis sit toti A B. manifestum fit, quòd
signum G prius pertransibit C B, quàm A C.
quo quidem pacto simul deprehenditur ibi motus
secundum partes temporis, & secundum partes rei
mobilis.
Potestne motus ita diuidi, ut non
etiam aliæ res simul diui-
dantur?
Non potest. Quando enim omne quod mouetur,
necessum [?]

page.notes: The diagram in the paragraph beginning "Sumatur": brackets join A to B and E to F, with G printed between the two lines above the second bracket. Brackets are shown here only as approximate symbols. A stray mark "i" stands at the left of the last line, below "mouetur"; it is not a catchword and is not transcribed. The word "necessum" is read from a worn ligature and is marked [?]. The heading "Potest' ne" has an apostrophe after "Potest" as printed. No catchword or signature is visible at the foot.
